parole.significato: An essential oil extracted from flowers.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Persian عطر (atr, “scent”), from Arabic عِطْر (ʕiṭr, “perfume”).

parole.significato: A large Central Asian frame drum with jingles attached, a type of tambourine.
parole.testo: From Persian دایره (dâyere), from Arabic دَائِرَة (dāʔira). Doublet of daerah.
Borrowed from Persian گزنگبین (gazangabin), from گز (gaz, “tamarisk”) + انگبین (angabin, “honey(dew)”). The variant is from its Arabic form جَزَنْجَبِين (jazanjabīn).
Borrowed from Persian حُجَّتُالْاِسلام (hojjatoleslâm), from Arabic حُجَّةُ ٱلْإِسْلَامِ (ḥujjatu l-ʔislāmi, literally “authority on Islam”)

parole.significato: Of or relating to Omar Khayyám (1048–1131), Persian polymath, philosopher, mathematician, astronomer and poet.
parole.testo: From Khayyam (from Persian خیام (xayyâm), from the Arabic male given name خَيّام (ḵayyām)) + -ian.

parole.significato: A Sufi Muslim who styles themselves after the Sufi mystic Rumi; a member of the Whirling Dervishes.
parole.testo: From Persian مولویه, Classical Persian مولوی (mawlawī), noun use of Arabic مَوْلَوِيّ (mawlawiyy, “of a lord or master”), ultimately from مَوْلًى (mawlan, “master”). Compare maulvi, mullah, maulana.

parole.significato: A title denoting the rank of a high nobleman or prince, signifying a male-line descent and relationship to the Imperial…
parole.testo: From Persian میرزا (mirzâ), from earlier میرزاد (mirzâd), composed of میر (mir, “commander”) (from Arabic title أَمِير (ʔamīr, “commander, prince”)) and the suffix ـزاد، ـزاده (-zâd, -zâde, “child of, son of”), from زادن (zâdan). Akin to Amir, amir, emir and admiral.

parole.significato: The native captain of an Indian cavalry regiment.
parole.testo: From Hindustani contraction रिसालदार (risāldār) / رسالدار (risāldār), from रिसालादार (risālādār) / رسالہ دار (risāla-dār), from Persian رسالهدار (resâle-dâr), from Arabic رِسَالَة (risāla) + Persian agent suffix دار (dâr).

parole.significato: A traditional lute-like musical instrument of Central Asia.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Persian رُبَاب, from Arabic رُبَاب (rubāb), plural of رَبَابَة (rabāba); similar forms exist in many languages where the instrument is played, such as Pashto رَبَاب (rabāb), Punjabi ਰਬਾਬ (rabāb) / رَبَاب (rabāb), Hindustani (Hindi रबाब (rabāb) / Urdu رَبَاب (rabāb)).
From Persian شهاب (šahâb, literally “meteor”), from Arabic شِهَاب (šihāb).
From Persian شراب (šarâb, “wine”), from Arabic شَرَاب (šarāb, “wine, beverage”), from شَرَبَ (šaraba, “to drink”).

parole.significato: The delegation of the power of divorce by the husband to the wife or any other party.
a type of vocal ornamentation; especially the variant used in the Near and Middle East
parole.testo: Borrowed from Persian تحریر (tahrir), from Arabic تَحْرِير (taḥrīr, “liberation; release”).
